title: Power Automate: share Process license capacity across cloud flows with flow groups
summary: The licensing, capacity limits, maker path and Dataverse creation call are supported by Microsoft documentation. Some governance checklist checks have no corresponding controls-table row, but no finding requires holding the briefing.

claims.claim: Flow groups share Process license capacity across multiple cloud flows instead of licensing each separately.
claims.quote: A flow group lets you share the capacity of a Power Automate Process license across multiple cloud flows, instead of dedicating a license to each flow separately.

claims.claim: A flow group can contain up to 25 flows.
claims.quote: A group can contain up to 25 solution-aware cloud flows.

claims.claim: Eligible cloud flows must be solution-aware, stored in a solution.
claims.quote: Cloud flows stored in a solution (solution-aware).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each Process license provides up to 250,000 actions per day.
claims.quote: Each Process license includes up to 250,000 actions per day (shown as Power Platform Requests in admin center reports).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: All flows in a group share a single 250,000-action daily pool.
claims.quote: When you assign it to a flow group, all flows in the group share that 250,000-action daily pool.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Consumption is measured against the group total rather than each individual flow.
claims.quote: Consumption is measured against the group total, not per individual flow.

claims.claim: A flow group is scoped to a single environment.
claims.quote: Scope | Single environment

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A flow group takes one Process license.
claims.quote: Process licenses per group | 1 (250,000 actions per day). Stacking isn't available for flow groups.

claims.claim: Process license stacking is not available for flow groups.
claims.quote: License stacking (assigning multiple Process licenses for higher capacity) isn't available for flow groups.

claims.claim: A flow can belong to only one group at a time.
claims.quote: Group membership | A flow can belong to only one group at a time

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Adding a parent flow does not automatically add its child flows.
claims.quote: Parent and child flows are separate group members; adding a parent flow to a group doesn't add its child flows automatically.

claims.claim: Each explicitly added parent or child flow counts separately toward the 25-member limit.
claims.quote: 25 total flow members. Each parent or child flow you add to the group counts separately.

claims.claim: Cloud flows not in a solution are not eligible.
claims.quote: Not eligible | Cloud flows not in a solution

claims.claim: Desktop flows are not eligible.
claims.quote: Not eligible ... Desktop flows (RPA)

claims.claim: Business process flows are not eligible.
claims.quote: Not eligible ... Business process flows

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Flows already covered by a per-user Power Automate plan are not eligible.
claims.quote: Not eligible ... Flows already covered by a per-user Power Automate plan

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and no other clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The record gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: Learn describes rollout starting in July 2026.
claims.quote: Flow groups start rolling out in July 2026.

claims.claim: The feature becomes available automatically without admin action to enable it.
claims.quote: The feature becomes available automatically; no admin action is required to enable it.

claims.claim: An environment without the Flow groups option has not yet received the feature.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Flow groups option yet, it didn't reach your environment. Check back as the rollout continues across regions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Group use is maker-opt-in: makers create a group and explicitly add flows before those flows use shared capacity.
claims.quote: Only flows that you explicitly add to the group use its shared Process capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that existing flows change automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups disable feature tenant environment admin switch existing flows automatically; flow groups data access existing price. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group; they describe explicit creation and membership, not automatic conversion.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Creating a flow group requires available Process license capacity in its environment.
claims.quote: A Power Automate Process license with available capacity in the environment. (You must have available Process capacity to assign when you create the group in Power Automate.)

claims.claim: Learn lists Power Automate maker permissions as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Prerequisites ... Power Automate maker permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature pages and flowgroup reference do not name the specific security roles entitled to create or change flowgroup records.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flowgroup table security roles create write permissions approval Process license assign. Read flow-groups, create-flow-group, flowgroup and security-roles-privileges; no flowgroup-specific named roles are given.

claims.claim: The documentation checked does not describe a separate flow-group approval step.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flowgroup table security roles create write permissions approval Process license assign. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group; their prerequisites and creation procedure give no separate approval step.

claims.claim: Learn describes license-capacity assignment but no new data access from flow groups.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups data access existing price. Opened flow-groups, create-flow-group and flowgroup table; they document capacity sharing, membership and group records, not a new data-access capability.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Removing a flow's Process license removes it from its group and breaks associations.
claims.quote: Removing a flow's Process license or switching it to a different plan removes the flow from its group and breaks any associations.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Switching a flow to a different plan removes it from its group.
claims.quote: Removing a flow's Process license or switching it to a different plan removes the flow from its group and breaks any associations.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Flows dependent on the group's Process capacity are suspended until relicensed after those license changes.
claims.quote: Flows that depended on the group's Process capacity are suspended until relicensed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Group membership is environment-specific and does not automatically transfer in managed-solution or pipeline deployments.
claims.quote: Flow group membership and Process license assignments are environment-specific. They don't transfer automatically when you deploy flows through managed solutions or pipelines.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Process license assignments are environment-specific and do not automatically transfer in managed-solution or pipeline deployments.
claims.quote: Flow group membership and Process license assignments are environment-specific. They don't transfer automatically when you deploy flows through managed solutions or pipelines.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A child flow left outside the group does not inherit its parent's shared capacity.
claims.quote: The child flow doesn't inherit the group's Process capacity from its parent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Automate Process is a paid capacity license.
claims.quote: License name | Power Automate Process ... License type | Capacity license (paid)

claims.claim: The add-on entitlement classification reflects the separately purchased Process capacity required for groups.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Creating a group fails when its environment has no available Process capacity.
claims.quote: If you see "Failed to create flow group: PowerAutomatePerProcess capacity … is 0," the environment has no available Process license capacity. Add Process licenses to the environment first.

claims.claim: Process licenses cannot currently be used in a pay-as-you-go environment.
claims.quote: You can't currently use Process licenses in a pay-as-you-go environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs flows needing Process entitlement to an environment not linked to an Azure subscription, with the license assigned to the flow or its group.
claims.quote: keep it in an environment that isn't linked to an Azure subscription and assign a Process license to the flow or to a flow group that contains it.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The flow-group pages publish no separate price for flow groups.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions; flow groups data access existing price. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group in full; neither gives a separate flow-group price.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The flow-group pages name no separate flow-group billing meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group in full; they give shared Process action entitlement, not a separate flow-group meter.

claims.claim: The flow-group pages name no separate flow-group license beyond Process capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group in full; Process capacity is named, with no separate flow-group license.

claims.claim: The flow-group pages themselves give no price for the Process license.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups data access existing price; Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Opened flow-groups and create-flow-group; neither states a Process license price.

claims.claim: Learn directs flows needing more than 250,000 daily actions to Process licenses assigned directly to the individual flow.
claims.quote: If a flow needs more than 250,000 actions per day, assign Process licenses directly to that individual flow instead.

claims.claim: A flow's Analytics page can be used to check daily action usage.
claims.quote: Open the cloud flow in Power Automate. Select Analytics on the flow's detail page. Review the Actions chart for the flow's average daily action count over the last 28 days.

claims.claim: Learn describes predictable, moderate-usage flows as good grouping candidates.
claims.quote: Good candidates for grouping have predictable, moderate usage (for example, 5,000–50,000 actions per day each).

claims.claim: Learn mentions regularly exceeding 100,000 daily actions as a reason to consider dedicated Process capacity.
claims.quote: If a flow regularly exceeds 100,000 actions per day, it might be better served by a dedicated Process license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends regularly reviewing consumption and moving a consistently dominant member to a dedicated Process license.
claims.quote: Review consumption regularly. If one flow consistently dominates the group's capacity, move it out and assign a dedicated Process license to that flow.

claims.claim: Flow-group creation is reached in Power Automate through environment > More > Flow groups > New flow group.
claims.quote: Select the environment that contains your Process licenses and solution flows. On the left navigation, select More > Flow groups. ... Select New flow group.

claims.claim: POST <organization-uri>/api/data/v9.2/flowgroups creates a Dataverse flowgroup row.
claims.quote: Create ... POST /flowgroups ... EntitySetName | flowgroups. Linked create-entity-web-api: Send a POST request to the Web API entityset resource to create a table row; POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/accounts.

claims.claim: The documented group-row creation call does not specify assigning Process capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: flowgroup table security roles create write permissions approval Process license assign. Read flowgroup writable columns and create-flow-group: POST /flowgroups has no documented capacity-assignment property.

claims.claim: No tenant or environment switch to disable the flow-groups feature is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups disable feature tenant environment admin switch existing flows automatically; flow groups disable Power Platform API PowerShell. Read create-flow-group, flowgroup and Disable-AdminFlow excerpts; no feature-wide switch found.

claims.claim: The flowgroup table reference documents an update operation.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /flowgroups(flowgroupid)

claims.claim: Learn recommends the Power Platform admin center Power Automate usage report for deciding which flows need dedicated capacity or can share a group.
claims.quote: Admins can use Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Power Automate > Usage ... The report helps you decide which flows need dedicated capacity and which can share a group.

claims.claim: The Usage page is a report, not a documented control that sets a consumption limit.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Opened power-automate-usage-report in full; its operations show usage and user/flow detail, not a setting to impose limits.

claims.claim: The Usage page shows consumption attributed to users.
claims.quote: The Usage page currently shows consumption attributed to users.

claims.claim: The Usage page does not show consumption attributed to service principals.
claims.quote: It doesn't show consumption attributed to service principals or flows covered by Process or legacy Per-flow licenses.

claims.claim: The Usage page omits flows covered by Process licenses.
claims.quote: It doesn't show consumption attributed to service principals or flows covered by Process or legacy Per-flow licenses.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The flow-group pages do not specify what happens to other members when the group's shared pool is exceeded.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Read flow-groups, create-flow-group and FAQ action-limit excerpts; generic per-flow throttling is documented, but group-overage treatment of other members is not specified.

claims.claim: Learn says rollout continues across regions but gives no regional completion dates.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups exceeded 250000 actions capacity limit throttle price meter rollout regions. Opened create-flow-group and flow-groups; July 2026 start and continued regional rollout are stated, with no completion dates.

claims.claim: All controls that the governance checklist asks readers to set or check have corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Identify candidate flows by their daily action count ... Create the group ... and add each parent and child flow explicitly ... Review group consumption regularly ... The Analytics usage check and the regular group-consumption review ... have no monitoring row
claims.fix: The checklist's Analytics check, regular group-consumption review, member-flow additions and dedicated-license assignments have no corresponding controls-table rows. This is a checklist/table coverage finding, not a request to add rows.

claims.claim: The documented group-row creation call does not specify adding member flows.
claims.quote: Searched: flowgroup table security roles create write permissions approval Process license assign; flow groups data access existing price. Read flowgroup writable columns and create-flow-group: POST /flowgroups has no documented member-addition property.

claims.claim: The flowgroup table reference documents a delete operation.
claims.quote: Delete ... DELETE /flowgroups(flowgroupid)

claims.claim: The flowgroup table reference documents a retrieve operation.
claims.quote: Retrieve ... GET /flowgroups(flowgroupid)

claims.claim: The Usage page omits flows covered by legacy Per-flow licenses.
claims.quote: It doesn't show consumption attributed to service principals or flows covered by Process or legacy Per-flow licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Process capacity licenses are purchased in addition to user licenses.
claims.quote: In addition to user licenses, organizations can upgrade their automation scenarios with capacity licenses
